input.question: Design a biochemical concentration-response experiment to measure inhibition of Interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 1 (P51617) by CHEMBL1738757. Propose an ordered procedure, justify the assay format and parameters, and explicitly identify unsupported conditions; do not supply a remembered potency.

step_cards.action: Prepare a compound dilution series and vehicle/reference controls.
Combine compound, kinase, substrate and ATP; run the reaction under justified conditions.
For ADP-Glo: stop the reaction and deplete residual ATP, then perform the ADP detection reaction and measure luminescence.
Prepare the specified cell system, dilution series, vehicle, reference and background controls.
Expose cells to compound under justified culture conditions.
For CellTiter-Glo: apply the ATP-based viability reagent, mix and stabilize according to a supported procedure, then measure luminescence.
Normalize against appropriate controls, fit a concentration-response curve, and report uncertainty and assay limitations.

retained_measurement_examples.description: HotSpot Assay: Table 3 and 4: The HotSpot kinase profiling and screening assays were carried out using the method of Anastassiadis et al., Nat. Biotechnol. (2011) Vol. 29, No. 11, pp. 1039-1045 (which is herein incorporated by reference in its entirety); 10 uM was the starting concentration with a 3-fold series dilution (10 doses) and the final ATP concentration was 10 uM.

IC50 Kinase Assays: Table 8-10: Compounds were tested in 10-dose IC50 mode with 3-fold serial dilution starting at 10 uM, and are relative to DMSO, the negative control. The positive control, Staurosporine, was tested in a 10-dose IC50 mode with 4-fold serial dilution starting at 20 uM. Reactions were carried out at 10 uM ATP. Curve fits were performed to determine IC50 where the enzyme activities at the highest concentration of compounds were less than 65%.

guidelines: Match the biological system and readout to the question.
